::: {.chapter-lead}
This page is the first stop (1 of 5) of the guided tour of the reference code: the smallest file of the package, the one that defines **what the model is** before any other file defines **what it does**. Every code excerpt is commented line by line; the full source lives in [`src/llm_lab/foundations/gpt_config.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/gpt_config.py).
:::
::: {.callout-note .learning-outcomes collapse="true" title="Learning outcomes"}
By the end of this tour, you will be able to:
- name every configuration dimension and what it determines elsewhere in the model;
- map each field to the tensor shapes it controls;
- explain why validation fails early with a named message instead of late with a shape error.
:::

## The file's role in the module family

The reference implementation is split into five modules, in reading order:

| Module | Contents | Tour page |
|---|---|---|
| `gpt_config.py` | dimensions, their names, their validation | this page |
| `gpt_ops.py` | numerical building blocks (init, projection, normalization, GELU) | [next](gpt-ops-walkthrough.qmd) |
| `transformer_block.py` | one complete pre-LN Transformer block | [block](transformer-block-walkthrough.qmd) |
| `gpt.py` | the assembled model: embeddings, blocks, output | [model](gpt-model-walkthrough.qmd) |
| `generate.py` | the autoregressive decoding loop | [generation](gpt-generation-walkthrough.qmd) |

Isolating configuration in one small immutable object has three pedagogical benefits: **one definition site** (every surprising dimension has a name here), errors **at construction time** (instead of a broadcasting crash mid-forward-pass), and **reproducibility** (two identically configured models are identical).

## The declaration: a frozen dataclass

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GPTConfig:
```

- `@dataclass` generates the constructor: no need to write six assignments by hand.
- `frozen=True` makes the object **immutable**. The configuration is read everywhere and written nowhere: "did something mutate the config mid-run?" becomes a guarantee instead of a debugging session. Any accidental assignment raises `FrozenInstanceError` immediately.

## The seven fields, one by one

```python
    vocab_size: int
    context_length: int
    embedding_dim: int
    num_heads: int
    num_layers: int
    mlp_hidden_dim: int
    seed: int = 0
```

| Field | Role | What it determines elsewhere |
|---|---|---|
| `vocab_size` (`V`) | vocabulary size | rows of the embedding table; number of logits per position |
| `context_length` (`T`) | maximum positions per pass | rows of the position table; width of the sliding generation window |
| `embedding_dim` (`d`) | residual-stream width | must be divisible by `num_heads`: each head owns `d/H` contiguous columns |
| `num_heads` (`H`) | number of attention heads | multi-head attention = `H` independent single-head attentions over slices |
| `num_layers` | depth (stacked blocks) | also scales the initialization of residual-path weights |
| `mlp_hidden_dim` | MLP hidden width | GPT-2 uses `4 * d`; here the value is explicit, hence visible and changeable |
| `seed` | initialization seed | inference is deterministic; the seed controls only the initial draws |

::: {.callout-note}
**Why does `seed: int = 0` have a default?** The other six dimensions describe the architecture; the seed describes an experiment. A default lets you build the model without thinking about it, then change it and observe that only the parameter values change — never the shapes, never the mechanics.
:::

## The validation: fail early, with a name

```python
    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        dimensions = {
            "vocab_size": self.vocab_size,
            "context_length": self.context_length,
            "embedding_dim": self.embedding_dim,
            "num_heads": self.num_heads,
            "num_layers": self.num_layers,
            "mlp_hidden_dim": self.mlp_hidden_dim,
        }
        for name, value in dimensions.items():
            if value <= 0:
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer")
        if self.embedding_dim % self.num_heads != 0:
            raise ValueError("embedding_dim must be divisible by num_heads")
```

Line by line:

- `__post_init__` runs **automatically at the end of the generated constructor**: the last moment when the caller still knows which value is wrong.
- The `dimensions` dict ties each value to **its field name**; without it, this would be six near-identical checks.
- `raise ValueError(f"{name} ...")`: the message names the culprit (`"vocab_size must be a positive integer"`) instead of a distant `shapes not aligned`.
- The **divisibility** check stands apart: multi-head attention slices the residual stream into `H` equal parts of `d/H` columns. A `d` that does not divide would make the split impossible — the failure would otherwise surface as a shape error in the middle of the first forward pass.

::: {.callout-warning}
**Common misconception.** `context_length` is not "the maximum output size". It is the number of **positions** the model can process in one pass; generation can produce longer sequences by sliding the window (see the `generate.py` tour).
:::

## What the tests verify

[`tests/unit/test_gpt_config.py`](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/tests/unit/test_gpt_config.py) checks exactly this file's promises: zero or negative dimensions are rejected with the right message, divisibility is enforced, the object is genuinely immutable (`FrozenInstanceError`), and the seed defaults to `0`.

## Exercises

1. What error do you get with `embedding_dim=10, num_heads=4`? And with `embedding_dim=12, num_heads=4`?
2. How many entries does the position table of a `context_length=256, embedding_dim=64` configuration have?

<details>
<summary>Show answers and reasoning</summary>

1. `10 % 4 == 2`: divisibility fails, so `ValueError` at construction. With `12 % 4 == 0`: accepted, and each head receives `12/4 = 3` columns.
2. `256 × 64 = 16384` values, i.e. 16384 learned parameters — one per position and per dimension. This count is independent of the vocabulary and the head count.
</details>
